chunks: Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd narrated from al-Dawa' ibn Farqad, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

[It is written] in the book of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): When you employ what your right hand possesses for something that is difficult for them, then work with them in it. He [the narrator] said: And indeed, you would instruct them, saying: 'Stay as you are,' then he would come and look. If it was heavy [difficult], he would say: 'In the name of Allah,' then he would work with them; and if it was light, he would step aside from them.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ethical guideline for masters working with slaves or employees?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elaborates on the prophetic tradition of equitable labor distribution, emphasizing that masters should share the burden of difficult tasks rather than merely commanding slaves, reflecting the Shia emphasis on humility and shared hardship. The text details a practical assessment of workload: if the task is heavy, the master joins in after invoking God's name; if light, he steps aside, illustrating a nuanced approach to justice and mercy in domestic and economic relations. This practice underscores the spiritual value of manual labor for leaders and the ethical obligation to alleviate the physical strain on dependents.
